2608.14036.title: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work-Until They Don't
2608.14036.paper_summary: Skills have emerged as a practical and effective approach for enhancing LLM agents at inference time through structured packages of knowledge. However, existing evaluations largely measure whether skills improve aggregated task success, leaving a more fundamental question underexplored: \emph{\textbf{When do skills help, why do they work, and where do they fail?}} Through controlled experiments across various benchmarks, agent harnesses and LLMs, we isolate the effects of representation, outcome annotation, retrieval difficulty, and cross-framework robustness of skills. To further answer this question, we design a contrastive study that combines controlled quantitative experiments with paired trajectory analysis. We normalize 8,135 trial records from controlled experiments and retain 238 valid unique labels from 240 open-coded records. We consolidate these observations into a taxonomy of three high-level categories and twelve skill-use modes: skills work when noisy trajectories become procedural anchors that stabilize execution. Skills improve over Workflow Memory by 6.06 points in matched comparisons. Procedural anchoring accounts for 65.7\% of skill cases, versus 4.5\% for explicit knowledge injection, showing that skills stabilize action rather than inject missing facts. Retrieval is a separate bottleneck: as pools grow from 5 to 100, actual-use precision falls from 29.6\% to 3.3\%. Confusable distractors impair offline identification, yet downstream success remains stable; exact ground-truth invocation is neither sufficient nor necessary. Skills fail under brittle assumptions, incompatible contexts, or insufficient adaptation. These findings move evaluation beyond aggregate success rates and guide reliable self-evolving agents.
2608.14036.paper_summary_zh: 技能已成為透過結構化知識包在推理時增強 LLM 代理的一種實用且有效的方法。<lb/>然而，現有的評估主要測量技能是否提高了綜合任務成功率，留下了一個更根本的問題未被深入探討：\emph{\textbf{技能在何時有幫助，為什麼有效，在哪裡失敗？}}<lb/>通過在各種基準、代理工具和 LLM 上進行的控制實驗，我們隔離了表徵、結果註釋、檢索難度和技能的跨框架穩健性等因素的影響。<lb/>為了進一步回答這個問題，我們設計了一個對比研究，結合了控制的定量實驗和配對軌跡分析。<lb/>我們對控制實驗中的 8,135 條試驗記錄進行了標準化，並從 240 條開放編碼記錄中保留了 238 條有效的唯一標籤。<lb/>我們將這些觀察結果整合成三個高層次類別和十二種技能使用模式的分類法：當嘈雜的軌跡成為穩定執行的程序錨點時，技能就會發揮作用。<lb/>在匹配比較中，技能在工作流程記憶上提高了 6.06 分。<lb/>程序錨定占技能案例的 65.7\%，而明確知識注入僅占 4.5\%，顯示技能穩定行動而不是注入缺失的事實。<lb/>檢索是一個單獨的瓶頸：當池從 5 增長到 100 時，實際使用的精確度從 29.6\% 降至 3.3\%。<lb/>易混淆的干擾項會損害離線識別，但下游成功率保持穩定；精確的真實調用既不充分也不必要。<lb/>技能在脆弱的假設、不兼容的上下文或適應不足的情況下失敗。<lb/>這些發現使評估超越了綜合成功率，並指導可靠的自我進化代理。
